gaps.evidence: AGENCYOS_MASTER_DEVELOPMENT_PLAN.md §4.8 says these totals are "regenerated from the gap records whenever one changes" and are "not maintained by hand". No such generator exists in scripts/, and none is run by CI. gapTotals read 81 while gaps held 82; baseline read 30 migrations and 694 tests against an actual 36 and 895; findings listed D16-D22 as open after all seven had merged. A document that reports its own staleness as fact is the hazard directive §42 names.

adminDecisions.title: How long may a client who has paid in full wait for the next stage to open before somebody is told?
adminDecisions.why: D18 gave the retry ladder ~19 minutes of real spacing. After that the job is dead and nothing tries again. The ladder is an engineering default; the number is a business rule nobody has stated.

adminDecisions.title: Is supabase/_bundle.sql a supported install path?
adminDecisions.why: It is twelve migrations stale and ships the D19 defect. Either CI regenerates it on every migration, or it is deleted and `db push` is documented as the only way in. Keeping it as-is means the documented install produces a knowingly defective deployment.

adminDecisions.title: Does winning a deal qualify its lead, or must a lead be qualified before a deal can be won?
adminDecisions.why: Nothing requires a lead to be qualified before a deal is opened on it, so the ordinary path is new -> deal won -> converted. LEAD_TRANSITIONS says only qualified may become converted. Both cannot be true. D20 preserved today's behaviour rather than pick.

adminDecisions.title: When a past client comes back, is that a new deal on the same lead, or a new lead?
adminDecisions.why: WhatsApp ingest keys a lead to a phone number permanently, so a returning client lands on the same lead row. D21 stopped the schema from forbidding a second deal there, but createOpportunity still returns the settled one instead of raising a new one. Which behaviour is right is a sales-process question.

adminDecisions.title: Who may change a deal's value after it is opened, and is a change of price audited?
adminDecisions.why: value_minor is written at insert and never updated, and convertToProject seeds the project budget from it. A reopened deal re-won at a different figure converts into a project budgeted at the old one.

adminDecisions.title: Merge approval for PR #40 (G-079, audit written in the transaction it describes)
adminDecisions.why: The convention this project has kept is one merge-approval decision per pull request. PR #40 had none. audit.audit_log is append-only by trigger, so a history row that is never written can never be repaired later; the four call sites with a Postgres function to sit inside no longer take that risk. Granted 2026-08-12; merged as 9874f14.
